name: KFC
problem: App engagement wasn't turning into in-store and kiosk orders.
Each market ran CRM differently, so wins didn't travel.
Loyalty had to work across app, kiosk and delivery.
built: Journeys linking app activity to in-store redemption.
Reusable templates for faster market rollouts.
Gamified, loyalty-led campaigns with redemption tracking.
measured: Time to launch in a new market

name: Shell
problem: Customers came for fuel but rarely went into the store.
Fuel, store and loyalty data sat in separate systems.
Promotions weren't timed to the visit.
built: Single customer view feeding Braze from the warehouse.
Visit- and location-triggered offers to move forecourt traffic in-store.
Segments built on visit frequency and basket.

name: Zerion
problem: New wallet users dropped before their first meaningful action.
Product events weren't structured for CRM use.
Tight timeline to go live.
built: Event and attribute schema for lifecycle messaging.
Onboarding journeys guiding users to first transaction.
Phased launch to deliver value within weeks.

name: Back Market
problem: Long gaps between purchases made customers forget the brand.
Broad sends with declining engagement.
Little personalisation by device owned.
built: Post-purchase journeys for accessories, care and trade-in.
Segments by category and device lifecycle.
Win-back timed to upgrade cycles.

name: Creative Assembly
problem: Player data fragmented across titles and platforms.
Lapsed players got the same messages as active ones.
Hard to tie comms to in-game engagement.
built: Unified player profiles for cross-title segments.
Journeys by player stage: new, active, lapsing, lapsed.
Event-triggered messages on in-game milestones.

name: FIVE Hotels
problem: Guests booked through OTAs, so the hotel owned little of the relationship.
Minimal pre-arrival and post-stay contact.
Guest data split across booking and property systems.
built: Pre-arrival, in-stay and post-stay journeys.
Upsell moments for dining, spa and experiences.
Re-booking journeys to grow direct bookings.

name: Huckleberry
problem: Free users weren't reaching the moment premium felt essential.
Parents' needs change fast as a child ages.
Generic content didn't match each family's stage.
built: Age- and stage-based lifecycle journeys.
Upgrade prompts at high-intent moments.
Trial-to-paid journeys with value reminders.

name: Hand & Stone
sector: Massage and facial spa franchise, US
problem: Membership drives revenue, and early churn erodes it.
Hundreds of locations, each with its own data and booking patterns.
First-visit guests weren't consistently converted to members.
built: Intro-visit to membership conversion journeys.
Churn-risk signals from booking gaps and unused credits.
Location-aware messaging for franchisees.
